clue.text: Vegetable served after a special introduction to Alan Sugar backfired

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening letter, so only the start of Alan is used
something that backfires comes back the wrong way, so the word sugar is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Lord Sugar's TV dinner goes wrong, with a vegetable served after a fancy introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alan Sugar' reads as the businessman's name, but the two words are split between different jobs; 'backfired' makes RAGUS. Alan Sugar is a British tycoon from TV's The Apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: A green spear-shaped shoot eaten as a vegetable, typically served steamed with butter.

clue.text: Enlightened American overcoming battle with drug

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting over the rest comes first

parts.note: a war is a large-scale battle or conflict
E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A US veteran is changed by fighting and drugs into a more enlightened person.
explanation.definitionFit: Being informed or knowing about something is one sense of enlightened, a close synonym.

clue.text: Hairstyle involving plait twisted around bottom parts of wig

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are put round the other piece
twisted letters are bent out of their order, so plait is rearranged
in a down clue the bottom of a word is its end, so its last two letters are taken

explanation.surface: A hairdresser describes a style made by twisting a plait round the lower part of a wig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' makes P...TAIL, split to go 'around' the other piece; in a down clue 'bottom' means the end of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A single plait of hair hanging down the back of the head is a named hairstyle.

clue.text: Bar set up for merrymaking

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting a word up writes it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a lever is a bar used to prise or lift

explanation.surface: A pub is being prepared for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub to be set up for drinking, but it is a crowbar, a LEVER, which 'set up' turns over.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively, noisy festivity is merrymaking, and that is what a revel is.

clue.text: Boss detailed to catch Irish animal

indicators.note: the shortened word catches the other piece inside it
detailed is read as de-tailed: the final letter is removed

parts.note: gaffer is British slang for a boss or foreman

explanation.surface: A boss is told in detail to catch an animal from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' is a pun on de-tailed, cutting a final letter to leave GAFFE, which 'to catch' wraps round the other piece. Gaffer is everyday British slang for a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-necked African mammal is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Submit to European rule after university clergyman's in post

indicators.note: the European rule pieces come after the rest
the university and clergyman pieces go inside the word for post

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title; the 's is read as 'is'
R is a standard abbreviation for rule, as in R for rex or regina

explanation.surface: A college chaplain in a new post is told to accept European rule.
explanation.walkthrough: Right Reverend is the formal title of an Anglican bishop; 'post' is the verb, to mail, not a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender is to give in or yield, which is a sense of submit.

clue.text: Right to withdraw from deal with milk supplier

indicators.note: the letter for right is pulled out of the longer word

parts.note: to treat a matter is to deal with it

explanation.surface: Someone has the right to pull out of a deal involving a dairy farmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nipple on an udder is where a calf or kid draws its milk from.

clue.text: Options shown here for sailor accepting request by bishop

indicators.note: the sailor's word takes the other pieces into it

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
to ask is to request
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A sailor puts in a request for a bishop, and options are offered.
explanation.definitionFit: On a computer screen, the strip of icons for launching or switching programs presents the user's options.

clue.text: Teenager prepared to accept central part of farmer's contract …

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in the other piece
letters that are prepared are made up into something new, so teenager is rearranged
the middle letter of farmer's, counting all seven characters

explanation.surface: A teenager gets ready to sign a deal with a farmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' makes AGREEENT from TEENAGER, and 'to accept' puts M, the centre of farmer's, inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract is a binding arrangement between parties, a formal kind of agreement.

clue.text: European city home to heart of religious relic

indicators.note: the city houses the other piece inside it

parts.note: Hanover is a city in northern Germany

indicators.note: the middle letter of religious, its fifth of nine

explanation.surface: A German city houses the core of a sacred relic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relic' looks like a holy object, but it is the definition: something left over from a past night.
explanation.definitionFit: A headache after heavy drinking is a lingering relic of the night before, a witty sideways sense.

clue.text: Herb wanting space in flower bed

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the space is taken out

parts.note: rosemary is an aromatic herb
an em is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: A herb needs room to grow in the garden border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'space' is the printing term EM, the width of a letter M.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosary can mean a rose garden, a bed planted with roses, beside its prayer-bead sense.

clue.text: Item found in dock?

definitions.meaning: a single particular or point within a whole
to dock an animal is to cut off its tail, read here as the answer

explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' looks like a harbour, but it is the verb for cutting off a tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A detail is an individual item, and to de-tail is to dock a tail.

clue.text: Cooks receiving letter about items on the house?

indicators.note: the word for cooks takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: to fry is to cook, so fries means cooks

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letter's name is read backwards

parts.note: bee is the spelt-out name of the letter B

explanation.surface: Chefs open a letter about dishes given away free by the restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' is a spelt-out letter name, which 'about' makes EEB; 'on the house' means given free by the establishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Things given away without charge, as a restaurant offers drinks on the house.

clue.text: Unpopular Soviet leader visiting a German POW camp …

indicators.note: unpopular is not in, so the letters spelling in are removed

parts.note: Stalin led the Soviet Union

explanation.surface: A hated Soviet leader visits a German prisoner-of-war camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unpopular' says 'not in', so STALIN loses IN to give STAL.
explanation.definitionFit: German camps for captured enlisted soldiers in the Second World War were known by this name.

clue.text: … but destroyed a giant hen

indicators.note: a destroyed phrase is broken apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing the story: a giant hen was wrecked, though.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 12 across, but the clue stands alone; 'but' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a contrary thought, just as 'however' or 'but' does.

clue.text: Ms Garland beaten in top score at the bridge table

definitions.text: top score at the bridge table

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Judy Garland loses at a bridge party.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, winning all thirteen tricks is the highest achievable result, earning a big bonus.

clue.text: … sanctioned over participating in the bombing of Dresden

indicators.note: the letter joins in, going inside the rearranged letters
bombing blows the word apart, so Dresden's letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Continuing from the ellipsis: the wartime bombing of Dresden was officially sanctioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the bombing of' rearranges DRESDEN into ENDRSED, and 'participating in' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a plan is to approve or authorise it, so sanctioned is a synonym.

clue.text: Elegant plot about broadcast

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for plot is read backwards

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot
something being broadcast is on air

explanation.surface: A conspiracy concerning a radio or TV programme is described as stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' reads as a scheme, but it is a garden BED, which 'about' turns into DEB.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes a confident, stylish and charming manner, especially in a man.

clue.text: Very large beetroot served with full-flavoured bird

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing label for very large
read as beet root: the root of beet is its bottom letter in a down clue
rich food is full-flavoured

explanation.surface: An enormous beetroot is served alongside a richly flavoured roast bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beetroot' splits as 'beet root', the last letter of beet.
explanation.definitionFit: The large flightless African runner is an example of a bird.

clue.text: A doctor trapped in station went on the rampage

indicators.note: the pieces are held inside the word for station

parts.note: rank and station both mean social position
MO is Medical Officer, an army doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor stuck at a railway station loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'station' reads as a railway stop, but it is RANK, standing in society.
explanation.definitionFit: To run wild in a frenzy, causing havoc, is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Discount English book with standard jacket

indicators.note: the word for standard wraps round the other pieces like a book jacket

parts.note: a rate is a standard or level

explanation.surface: An English book sold with a standard dust jacket is marked down.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebate is money returned or knocked off a price, so a reduction or discount.

clue.text: Upturned vessel containing a Catholic Church deity

indicators.note: the overturned vessel holds the other pieces
in a down clue an upturned word is written bottom to top

parts.note: a sub is a submarine, a type of vessel

explanation.surface: An overturned chalice in a Catholic church holds a sacred figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' reads as a chalice or bowl, but it is a SUB, which 'Upturned' makes BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of wine and revelry is one deity of classical mythology.

clue.text: No points awarded to amateur coming back for old elephant

indicators.note: coming back means the whole string runs in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
dots are small points
AM is a standard abbreviation for amateur

explanation.surface: An amateur scores nothing on a return to an elephant contest.

clue.text: Relish being fashion designer in large house

indicators.note: the designer's initials go inside the house

parts.note: a pile is a large, imposing house

explanation.surface: A fashion designer enjoys life in a mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relish' reads as enjoyment, but it is the definition: a condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickle is a condiment of preserved vegetables, which is a relish.

clue.text: Fish with rod

definitions.meaning: an old unit of length of five and a half yards, also called a pole

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish with rod' reads as angling; 'with' only links two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Perch is both a freshwater fish and an old measure equal to a rod.

clue.text: Clean dirty weapon

indicators.note: messing something up, or dirtying it, puts its letters in disorder

explanation.definitionFit: A long spear carried by a mounted knight is an example of a weapon.

clue.text: Book deal in trouble

explanation.surface: A book deal has run into difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' reads as reserving or a publishing deal, but it is the definition: a book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Daniel is one of the books of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Trader supposed to go round royal church

indicators.note: the word for supposed surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: meant, as in 'meant to be', means supposed

explanation.surface: A dealer is due to tour a royal chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant is someone who buys and sells goods, especially wholesale, so a trader.

clue.text: Moccasin chosen to cover part of foot

indicators.note: the words cover the answer, which sits inside them across the word break

explanation.surface: A moccasin is picked to protect part of the foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of foot' looks anatomical, but a foot here is the twelve-unit measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A foot contains twelve of these imperial units, so one is a part of a foot.

clue.text: Pal drinking shake ordered to get a move on

indicators.note: the friend takes the drink inside

parts.note: mate is British slang for a pal or friend

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A friend gulps down a milkshake ordered so as to hurry up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like a café order, but it is the signal to rearrange, giving KEHAS for 'drinking' to take in.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning to hurry up, the same as the definition's phrase.
